## Substantive publication

Rendered PR: `#111` — `Explain progressive AgentSight fleet loading`.

New canonical page: `/blog/how-agentsight-loads-agent-fleets-progressively/`, titled **How AgentSight keeps a multi-node agent fleet responsive when one Node is slow**.

The article is pinned to AgentSight v1.0.31 commit `bb99b66f8f98e4b9f8b1769a3da0a8fbbe26b6c3` and documents:

- concurrent per-Node fleet probes;
- per-Node `setFleetSamples` updates that become visible before the outer `Promise.all` settles;
- the distinction between progressive row visibility and the global end-of-refresh barrier;
- Direct/relay choice as per-Node state rather than a fleet-wide transport result;
- generation counters that prevent stale organization/fleet/active-Node results from overwriting newer state;
- dynamic process/analysis session views and tab-scoped analysis work;
- the 12-second default browser request timeout and 30-second session-request timeout;
- the read/write retry boundary that permits GET/HEAD fallback but does not automatically replay ambiguous writes;
- explicit non-claims: no authorization/Controller-policy change and no general device/network latency benchmark.

The Blog hub and CollectionPage JSON-LD now discover the article, and the sitemap includes the canonical route with a 6 September last-modified date. The Blog hub's own sitemap last-modified date was also refreshed to 6 September because its rendered content changed.
